verdict.reasoning: Doctor summarizes: "you've got a dry itchy rash on your, mainly your hands... and your arms which started, perhaps after swimming a few days ago."

Patient says skin is "quite red" and "really dry itchy"; location is arms and hands; when asked if it has spread to chest/legs/face there is no indication it has; patient states "I don't have any spots".

Patient: "no fever , and I'm not sweating either"; doctor: "No fevers? No vomiting?" Patient: "No"; bowels and urine are "OK"; appetite and eating/drinking are normal; patient: "I think I have been, quite tired."
Doctor: "no, problems of skin problems in the past, things like eczema or, um, dermatitis?" Patient: "Uh, no".
Patient: "I'm currently taking ..." Doctor clarifies: "Microgynon... it's a contraceptive pill" and patient agrees.
When asked about allergies, patient says: "I think, um, I might be lactose intolerant."
Patient: "my dad has asthma".
Patient: "and, my mum has hayfever."
Doctor: "any skin problems that you're aware of?" Patient: "Uh, no."

Patient: "I've been really stressed at work" and "I've been working really long hours"; confirms: "I work as a teacher" and later doctor specifies primary school teacher with patient: "Yes, that's right."
Patient confirms living alone: "Ohh, it's just me"; denies smoking, alcohol, and recreational drugs: "no, I don't smoke", "Uh, no" (alcohol), "No" (recreational drugs).
Patient: "I went swimming a few days ago" with symptoms starting after swimming; also: "I'm using coconut butter for the past few days" and when asked if it helped: "No".

Doctor states: "you may have something called dermatitis" and summarizes a "dry itchy rash" on hands and arms starting after swimming a few days ago, with "no other symptoms, you're feeling otherwise, well, no fevers"; patient had described it as "quite red" (erythematous) and dry (pruritic, erythematous, dry rash with no systemic symptoms).
Patient reports "really stressed at work" and "working really long hours" and later acknowledges feeling "quite tired."
Doctor: "we have steroid creams I can give you, um, which will help with the inflammation."

Doctor: "something called emollients, which can help with the dry, dry skin. And that's something you just need to kind of paste on, uh, on to your skin, uh, throughout the day for the next few days."
Doctor: "you can also try antihistamines, so you can get things over the counter, Piriton, Loratadine"; chlorphenamine is not mentioned, so including it is an unsupported addition.
Doctor: "I can give you a patient information leaflet about [dermatitis], which gives a bit more information about the disease."
Doctor: "Paracetamol on this occasion, wouldn't be helpful. Um, uh, uh, painkillers wouldn't be helpful , on this occasion."
Doctor: "if it's still not getting better, come back and see me next week, and we can have another look again, at your symptoms."
